title: Pepper Station: Returns assistant onramp - call journal
content:
Call summary:
- Date: 2025-02-12, 11:00am PT call with Pepper Station (jenna@pepperstation.com) + internal CS/Eng/Edge Ops. ~45m.
- Primary ask: deploy a returns-assistant (receipt parsing + refund recommendation) that sits behind their checkout portal; must meet latency <300ms p99 for summary endpoints and be PCI-conscious (no full-card persistence).

High-level customer context:
- Mid-market retail chain (~80 stores, heavy weekend spikes).
- Current returns flow: customer uploads photo of receipt -> manual ops -> refund decision. Goal: automate triage + suggested refund amount, not final decision.
- Data constraints: receipts are images + OCR -> structured line items. Pepper Station wants no raw card numbers ever leave their environment. They prefer Private deployment if feasible, but open to Dedicated if VPC/NAT routing meets their security team.

Notes from technical questions and answers:
- Jenna: concerned about token cost when long receipts + itemized lines. Ethan: we can suggest truncation + key-field extraction pre-tokenize; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization for their throughput.
- Rajiv: asked about streaming UI and partial responses for UX. Answer: hosted API supports streaming, but for Private we need to verify the console-agent websocket proxy. Add ENG ticket.
- Lina: asked whether model fallback (smaller LLM) is automatic. Answer: yes via routing policies but need to confirm semantic parity for suggestion quality; propose A/B canary.
- Security: Pepper Station requires KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and audit logs for every inference request. Confirmed for Private; Dedicated requires additional config (ENG checklist).

Observed gotchas / risk notes (actionable):
- OCR variability: many receipts have vendor-specific line breaks that blow tokenization. Suggest pre-processor to normalize line items (strip vendor marketing lines). Action: add minimal heuristics in ingestion to limit token length.
- Batching + p99 spikes: when we batch many short receipts, tail latency can spike if batching window is too aggressive during surge. For weekend spikes, recommend aggressive autoscale + conservative max_batch_wait (20ms) for the critical summary route.
- PCI surface area: avoid sending PAN even masked unless customer contractually allows. Recommend design where only last4 (masked) is kept in ephemeral request context and never logged. Add privacy review.
- Model hallucination on refund amounts: observed in internal tests where model invents discounts. Need eval prompt set that forces calibration to parsed line items. Add eval job.
- Edge deployment constraints: Pepper Station has on-prem kiosk devices that may call a regional edge proxy. Verify TLS mutual-auth for kiosk to edge.

Requirements checklist (from call):
- Must: p99 latency <300ms for summary endpoint during simulated 2k req/min peak.
- Must: No raw PANs persist or leave their VPC; KMS customer-managed keys.
- Must: Audit logs for every inference with request-id mapping to their internal ticketing.
- Should: Streaming partial suggestions to UI while final recommendation computed.
- Should: Canary rollout with 10% traffic, automatic fallback to older model on aggregated quality gap >5%.
- Nice-to-have: model suggestion confidence score and rationale snippets for CX review.

Preliminary architecture options discussed:
1) Private deployment (preferred by Jenna): Redwood Private with customer VPC peering, KMS integration, audit logs. Pros: meets security; Cons: longer lead time, infra procurement.
2) Dedicated (shorter lead): Reserved capacity hosted in Redwood infra + strict VPC NAT + KMS via our partner. Pros: faster; Cons: still involves trusting Redwood infra for PAN handling -> requires legal sign-off.
3) Hybrid: Dedicated for inference, but all OCR and tokenization pre-processing runs in customer infra and sends structured items only. This minimizes token surface area.

Immediate next steps / action items (owner, due):
- Maya: open privacy checklist ticket + schedule privacy review with security (due 2025-02-18). Related: JIRA CS-5812.
- Ethan: bench latency on representative receipts (we have sample set from Jenna) and produce p95/p99 matrix for two model sizes (base-7B quantized, base-13B) (due 2025-02-17). JIRA: ENG-9123.
- Rajiv: validate streaming support for Private websocket proxy and confirm mTLS for kiosk proxy (due 2025-02-19).
- Lina: draft canary rollout config (10% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback thresholds; propose in product-ops doc (due 2025-02-21).
- Jenna (customer): provide 200 representative receipts (anonymized) and example UI flow for streaming skeleton (due 2025-02-16).

Short-term experiments to reduce token cost:
- Implement simple pre-tokenizer to extract only: merchant name, date, total, line-item names + qty + price, taxes. Keep commentary lines out.
- Try prefix/KV caching for repeated merchant disclaimers so same header text doesn't pay tokens each time.
- Run evaluation with disabled hallucination prompts: force model to quote only parsed fields and fallback to "needs human review" if uncertain.

Notes-to-self (loose):
- Bring up legal about contract clause for PAN handling in Dedicated vs Private. Likely need addendum for Dedicated.
- Ask infra for estimated lead time for Private VPC onboarding (ballpark 6-8 weeks).
- Keep Pepper Station in trial Dedicated while Private onboarding proceeds; justify with hybrid ingestion pattern to keep PANs in their network.

Reference links pulled during call:
- Confluence: Pepper Station intake page (linked above)
- Internal bench notebook: GH PR #482 (serving-runtime tweaks for small-batch latency)
- Slack: thread #cs-pepperstation (contains sample receipts)

Longer-term product asks from customer (note - important for roadmap):
- A prebuilt receipts extraction pipeline inside Redwood Optimize that can be toggled per-customer (to reduce customer dev work).
- Built-in PCI-safe tokenization primitives that integrate with customer KMS and provide audit-ready logs.

Open questions to answer on follow-up:
- Can we get a reliable p99 under weekend weekend-surge pattern with autoscale only? (Ethan to test)
- Does Dedicated with strict VPC/NAT and our KMS-integration satisfy legal or do they insist on Private? (Maya to get legal answer)
- What's the rolling upgrade plan for model quantized variants (how do we measure quality drift quickly)? (Lina + Research to propose)

Quick meeting plan for next week:
- Wed 2025-02-19 9am PT: internal sync (CS + Eng + Security) to review bench numbers + privacy checklist outcomes.
- Fri 2025-02-21 10am PT: triage with Pepper Station to review canary plan and delivery timeline.

End journal entry.

Rough capture style intentionally messy — keep as ground truth for follow-up tickets and privacy/eng prework.
